title: Create a data set by hand
body:
Your local animal shelter tracks each dog's Name, Age, Weight, Color and whether it likes Cats. Create work.shelter from the rows below, one line per observation, and print it.

Pluto   3  25  Black    No
Lizzie  10 43  Tan      Yes
Pesci   10 38  Brindle  No
starter:
data work.shelter;

run;
hint: input Name $ Age Weight Color $ Cats $; then datalines;. A length statement stops "Brindle" from being cut to 8 characters.

title: Compute a new variable
body:
Create work.people with name, height_in and weight_lb from the data below. Add bmi = 703 * weight_lb / height_in**2, rounded to 0.1, and print the data set.

Asha 64 130
Bruno 70 185
Cleo 62 115
Dmitri 73 210
hint: Assignment statements go before datalines;. round(x, 0.1).

title: Several records on one line
body:
Create work.shelter2 with the same shelter data, but this time enter all three dogs on a single data line.

Pluto 3 25 Black No Lizzie 10 43 Tan Yes Pesci 10 38 Brindle No
starter:
data work.shelter2;

run;
hint: The double trailing @@ holds the line so the next iteration keeps reading from it.

title: Delimited data
body:
Read the #-delimited data below into work.shelter3.

Pluto#3#25#Black#No
Lizzie#10#43#Tan#Yes
Pesci#10#38#Brindle#No
starter:
data work.shelter3;

run;
hint: infile datalines dlm='#'; sets the delimiter for in-stream data.

title: Formats and labels
body:
Using the work.class data below:

  1. Use PROC FORMAT to create a format for grade: 0–59 F, 60–69 D, 70–79 C, 80–89 B, 90–100 A.
  2. In a DATA step, label bd as "Birthday", apply your grade format, and format bd with WORDDATE.
  3. Print the table with labels.
hint: proc format; value gradefmt 0-59='F' ...; run;. In the DATA step: label and format grade gradefmt. bd worddate.;. Use proc print ... label;.

title: Average two columns
body:
Create work.cars from sashelp.cars with a new variable mpg_average: the average of MPG_City and MPG_Highway. Print the first five observations of the three variables.

The course's Cars table is sashelp.cars (columns include Make, Type, Origin, MSRP, Horsepower, MPG_City, MPG_Highway). Write new tables to the WORK library.
hint: mean(a, b) or (a + b) / 2. Limit printing with the (obs=5) data set option.

title: Conditional character variable
body:
Add a character variable mpg_quality to work.cars: "Low" when mpg_average is under 20, "Medium" from 20 up to 30, "High" from 30 up. Print observations 65 through 70 for mpg_average and mpg_quality.

The course's Cars table is sashelp.cars (columns include Make, Type, Origin, MSRP, Horsepower, MPG_City, MPG_Highway). Write new tables to the WORK library.
hint: Set length mpg_quality $ 6; first, then if / else if / else. Print a range with (firstobs=65 obs=70).

title: Watch the length
body: Create work.groups from sashelp.class with age_group: "Pre-teen" when age is under 13, otherwise "Teen". Show a frequency table of age_group.
hint: SAS sets a character variable's length from its first value. Declare length age_group $ 8; first.

title: Write a SAS function
body:
Use PROC FCMP to create a function tier with one numeric argument that returns "Low" (under 20), "Medium" (20 to under 30) or "High" (30 and up). Use it to create mpg_quality2 from mpg_average and print observations 65–70.

The course's Cars table is sashelp.cars (columns include Make, Type, Origin, MSRP, Horsepower, MPG_City, MPG_Highway). Write new tables to the WORK library.
starter:
proc fcmp outlib=work.functions.myfuncs;

quit;
hint: function tier(x) $ 6; declares a character return. Point SAS at it with options cmplib=work.functions;.

title: Subset and stack tables
body:
Create sports (Make, Type, MSRP for Sports cars over $100,000) and suv (same columns, SUVs over $60,000). Then row-bind them into expensive and print it. You should get 6 rows.

The course's Cars table is sashelp.cars (columns include Make, Type, Origin, MSRP, Horsepower, MPG_City, MPG_Highway). Write new tables to the WORK library.
hint: keep= and where for each subset. Listing two tables in one SET statement stacks them.

title: One-way frequency table
body:
Generate a frequency table for Type in sashelp.cars. Are the vehicle types evenly distributed?

The course's Cars table is sashelp.cars (columns include Make, Type, Origin, MSRP, Horsepower, MPG_City, MPG_Highway). Write new tables to the WORK library.
hint: proc freq; tables var; run;

title: Conditional printing
body: From work.class, print student, country and grade for students from France with a grade above 79.
hint: where works inside PROC PRINT. Character comparisons are case-sensitive.

title: Summary by group
body: Using sashelp.class, report N, mean, minimum and maximum of height and weight for each sex, with one decimal place.
starter:
proc means data=sashelp.class;

run;
hint: Statistics go on the PROC statement with maxdec=1; then class and var.

title: Percentiles to a table
body:
Use PROC MEANS to compute the 10th percentile, median and 90th percentile of MSRP and Horsepower for each Origin. Save the results with ODS OUTPUT as summary_table and print it. Which origin has the highest median price?

The course's Cars table is sashelp.cars (columns include Make, Type, Origin, MSRP, Horsepower, MPG_City, MPG_Highway). Write new tables to the WORK library.
hint: ods output Summary=work.summary_table; before the PROC captures its Summary table.

title: Query with PROC SQL
body: List the name and age of students in sashelp.class who are 15 or older, oldest first, then by name.
starter:
proc sql;

quit;
hint: PROC SQL ends with quit;, not run;.

title: Unique levels
body: With PROC SQL, print the unique levels of country in work.class.
hint: select distinct.

title: Group averages
body:
With PROC SQL, show the number of cars and the average MSRP for each Origin in sashelp.cars, formatted as dollars, highest average first.

The course's Cars table is sashelp.cars (columns include Make, Type, Origin, MSRP, Horsepower, MPG_City, MPG_Highway). Write new tables to the WORK library.
starter:
proc sql;

quit;
hint: avg(MSRP) as avg_msrp format=dollar12. and group by Origin.

title: Store a value in a macro variable
body:
Use PROC SQL to store the median MSRP of sashelp.cars in a macro variable. Then create work.cars with msrp_bin = 1 when MSRP is above the median and 0 otherwise, and show a frequency table of msrp_bin.

The course's Cars table is sashelp.cars (columns include Make, Type, Origin, MSRP, Horsepower, MPG_City, MPG_Highway). Write new tables to the WORK library.
hint: select median(MSRP) into :med_msrp. Reference it as &med_msrp. A comparison like (MSRP > x) evaluates to 1 or 0.

title: Random numbers with a DO loop
body: Create work.rand with 10 observations and two random variables (one normal, one uniform). Use call streaminit with a seed of your choice, and print the data.
starter:
data work.rand;

run;
hint: Inside do i = 1 to 10; ... output; end;, use rand('normal') and rand('uniform').

title: Nested loops
body: Create a data table with the same two random variables, 10 rows in total: a variable Class that is 1 for the first five rows and 2 for the next five. Drop the inner loop index and add seq running from 1 to 10. Print the data.
hint: Outer loop over Class, inner loop 1 to 5, a counter seq + 1;, and drop=j.

title: PDF and CDF
body: Use a DO loop to create quantiles 0 to 10. For a binomial distribution with p = 0.8 and n = 10, create PDF and CDF. Then use the CDF to create Quantile, which should mirror the loop values. Print the result.
hint: pdf('binomial', q, p, n), cdf(...) and quantile('binomial', prob, p, n).

title: Simulate and plot
body: Create 1,000 random chi-square deviates with 20 degrees of freedom (seed 123). Plot a histogram with PROC SGPLOT using bin width 1, add normal and kernel density curves, the title "My Random Chi-Square Distribution", the x-axis label "Random Chi-Square Deviates", and x-axis limits 5 to 40.
hint: rand('chisquare', 20). In SGPLOT: histogram ... / binwidth=1;, two density statements, and xaxis label= min= max=.

title: Correlation
body: Use PROC CORR to get the correlation between height and weight in sashelp.class.
hint: proc corr; var ...; run;

title: Two-sample t-test
body: Use PROC TTEST to compare mean height between the sexes in sashelp.class.
hint: class names the grouping variable; var the outcome.

title: Multiple regression
body:
Fit a regression of MPG_Highway on Horsepower and Weight using sashelp.cars. Use ODS SELECT to show only the ANOVA, FitStatistics and ParameterEstimates tables, and save predicted values and residuals with an OUTPUT statement.

The course's Cars table is sashelp.cars (columns include Make, Type, Origin, MSRP, Horsepower, MPG_City, MPG_Highway). Write new tables to the WORK library.
hint: ods select ...; before the PROC. In PROC REG: model y = x1 x2; and output out= p= r=;.

title: One-way ANOVA
body:
Use PROC GLM to test whether mean MPG_Highway differs by vehicle Type in sashelp.cars, and request Tukey-adjusted pairwise comparisons of the means.

The course's Cars table is sashelp.cars (columns include Make, Type, Origin, MSRP, Horsepower, MPG_City, MPG_Highway). Write new tables to the WORK library.
hint: class Type; model y = Type; then lsmeans Type / adjust=tukey pdiff;.

title: Distribution and normality
body:
Use PROC UNIVARIATE to describe Cholesterol in sashelp.heart, request tests for normality, and draw a histogram with a fitted normal curve.

sashelp.heart is the Framingham Heart Study sample (5,209 rows) with columns including Status (Alive/Dead), Sex, AgeAtStart, Cholesterol, Systolic, Smoking.
hint: The NORMAL option on the PROC statement adds the tests; histogram var / normal; overlays the curve.

title: Means with confidence limits
body: Use PROC MEANS to report N, mean and the 95% confidence limits of MPG_Highway for each Origin in sashelp.cars.
hint: CLM requests two-sided confidence limits for the mean.

title: Chi-square test of association
body:
Use PROC FREQ to test whether Sex and Status are associated in sashelp.heart. Show the two-way table with row percents only.

sashelp.heart is the Framingham Heart Study sample (5,209 rows) with columns including Status (Alive/Dead), Sex, AgeAtStart, Cholesterol, Systolic, Smoking.
hint: tables a*b / chisq;. NOCOL NOPERCENT leave only row percents.

title: Nonparametric comparison
body: Use a Wilcoxon rank-sum test to compare height between the sexes in sashelp.class.
hint: PROC NPAR1WAY with the WILCOXON option.

title: Logistic regression
body:
Model the probability that Status is "Dead" in sashelp.heart from AgeAtStart, Cholesterol and Sex (reference level Female). Report odds ratios.

sashelp.heart is the Framingham Heart Study sample (5,209 rows) with columns including Status (Alive/Dead), Sex, AgeAtStart, Cholesterol, Systolic, Smoking.
hint: model Status(event='Dead') = ...; sets which outcome is modelled. Put Sex in a CLASS statement with ref=.

title: Stepwise model selection
body: Use PROC GLMSELECT on sashelp.cars to choose predictors of MPG_Highway from Horsepower, Weight, EngineSize, Cylinders, Wheelbase and Length with stepwise selection using significance level 0.05 to enter and to stay.
hint: selection=stepwise(select=sl sle=0.05 sls=0.05) on the MODEL statement.

title: Simulate process data
body: Create work.shafts with 25 subgroups of 5 shaft diameters each, drawn from a normal distribution with mean 25 and standard deviation 0.012 (seed 7, rounded to 0.0001). Subgroups 18 to 20 have a tool shift: add 0.025 to their diameters. Then report the overall mean and standard deviation.
hint: Nested DO loops with output; inside; rand('normal', mean, sd).

title: Cp and Cpk
body: Starting from work.shafts (code given), compute Cp = (USL − LSL) / 6σ and Cpk = min(USL − μ, μ − LSL) / 3σ with LSL = 24.95 and USL = 25.05. Use PROC MEANS with an OUTPUT statement, then a DATA step, and print the result.
hint: output out=... mean=mu std=sigma; writes one row of statistics you can compute with in a DATA step.

title: X-bar and R chart
body:
Draw X-bar and R control charts of diameter by subgroup for work.shafts (code given) and list any tests that are triggered.

This uses PROC SHEWHART from SAS/QC.
hint: xrchart process*subgroup; draws both charts. tests=1 to 8 applies the Western Electric run tests.

title: Control limits by hand
body: Without SAS/QC: compute each subgroup's mean and range from work.shafts (code given), then the centre line CL = mean of subgroup means and limits CL ± 0.577 × R̄. Print the subgroups whose mean is outside the limits.
hint: PROC MEANS with class subgroup; output out= mean= range=;, then join the per-subgroup table to a one-row summary in PROC SQL.

title: Defect rate by line and shift
body: Using work.defects (code given), use PROC SQL to report the total units, total defective and defect rate (formatted as a percent with 2 decimals) for each line and shift.
starter:
data work.defects;
   input line $ day shift $ units defective;
   datalines;
A 1 Day 520 12
A 1 Night 480 19
A 2 Day 510 10
A 2 Night 470 22
A 3 Day 530 14
A 3 Night 490 18
B 1 Day 600 9
B 1 Night 580 11
B 2 Day 610 8
B 2 Night 590 12
B 3 Day 605 10
B 3 Night 575 13
C 1 Day 450 20
C 1 Night 430 26
C 2 Day 460 18
C 2 Night 440 41
C 3 Day 455 22
C 3 Night 445 24
;
run;
solution:
data work.defects;
   input line $ day shift $ units defective;
   datalines;
A 1 Day 520 12
A 1 Night 480 19
A 2 Day 510 10
A 2 Night 470 22
A 3 Day 530 14
A 3 Night 490 18
B 1 Day 600 9
B 1 Night 580 11
B 2 Day 610 8
B 2 Night 590 12
B 3 Day 605 10
B 3 Night 575 13
C 1 Day 450 20
C 1 Night 430 26
C 2 Day 460 18
C 2 Night 440 41
C 3 Day 455 22
C 3 Night 445 24
;
run;

proc sql;
   select line, shift, sum(units) as units, sum(defective) as defective,
          sum(defective) / sum(units) as rate format=percent8.2
   from work.defects
   group by line, shift
   order by line, shift;
quit;
hint: Divide the sums, not the row rates. format=percent8.2 displays a percentage.

title: Pareto table
body: Defect causes this month were: scratch 48, dent 31, misalign 17, porosity 12, burr 6, other 4. Enter these counts with DATALINES and use PROC FREQ to list the causes from most to least frequent with cumulative percents.
hint: WEIGHT count; treats each row as that many observations; ORDER=FREQ sorts by frequency.

title: Capability analysis procedure
body:
Use PROC CAPABILITY on work.shafts (code given) with spec limits 24.95 and 25.05 and target 25 to report capability indices and a histogram with the spec limits drawn.

This uses PROC CAPABILITY from SAS/QC.
hint: The SPECS statement sets the limits; the indices table appears automatically.

title: OEE with PROC SQL
body:
Enter the machine log below with DATALINES. With PROC SQL, sum each machine's shifts and compute availability = (planned − downtime) / planned, performance = ideal_cycle_s × total / ((planned − downtime) × 60), quality = good / total and OEE = their product. Sort by OEE, highest first.

CNC1 480 35 30 780 765
CNC1 480 50 30 760 741
CNC1 480 20 30 820 806
CNC2 480 90 30 640 610
CNC2 480 60 30 700 676
CNC2 480 75 30 650 630
Press1 480 15 12 2100 2080
Press1 480 25 12 2050 2021
Press1 480 10 12 2180 2166
hint: In PROC SQL, refer to a column you just computed with the CALCULATED keyword.
